title: Telling the Truth About the Gap on My Resume
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Last month, I sat across from an interviewer who kept staring at the eighteen-month gap on my resume, clearly waiting for an explanation.
Narrator: A friend of mine had suggested, beforehand, that I simply say I was traveling, since that answer sounds confident and requires no further questions.
Narrator: [carefully] The truth, however, was that I left my previous job to care for my mother after her diagnosis, and I nearly didn't recover financially from that decision.
Narrator: If I told the traveling story, the interview would likely move on smoothly, and nobody would ever question it further.
Narrator: [reflective] Even so, sitting there, I decided I would rather explain the real reason and risk an awkward silence than build the job on a comfortable lie.
Narrator: So I explained it plainly, that my mother needed full-time care, and that I chose her over my career during that period without much hesitation.
Narrator: [honestly] The interviewer paused for a moment, and I genuinely couldn't tell whether that silence meant judgment or simply surprise at my directness.
Narrator: Then she said something I didn't expect, that she respected people who choose family over convenience, even when it costs them professionally.
Narrator: [seriously] We ended up talking for several extra minutes about caregiving, and the entire tone of the interview shifted into something far more genuine.
Narrator: I don't know yet if I got the position, and honestly, the honest answer might still work against me with a different interviewer.
Narrator: [gently] However, I realized that if a company only wants me because of a comfortable story, then it isn't really a place I want to work for long.
Narrator: I would rather be hired, or rejected, for exactly who I am and what I chose, than build a career on a small, convenient lie repeated for years.
Narrator: [encouraging] Despite the uncertainty, I walked out of that interview feeling steadier than I expected, as though I had finally stopped performing for a stranger's approval.
Narrator: Whatever the outcome turns out to be, at least this time, whoever hires me will actually know the person they are hiring.
